clips.send: Comparing two groups: plant heights without (A) and with (B) fertilizer, 10 random plants each. Mean A equals 11 cm, mean B equals 15 cm, and both have a mean absolute deviation (MAD) of 1.4 cm. The centers differ by 4 cm, almost 3 MADs, so the two piles overlap only a little: the fertilizer really seems to help.

clips.send: Here is a jar of 300 beads, some of them red. The whole jar is the population. What fraction is red? We could count every bead, but for a real population (every voter in a country, every fish in a lake) that is impossible.

clips.send: Now use bigger samples of 80 beads each. The new pile is much narrower: bigger samples vary less, so a single big sample is more likely to land close to the truth.

clips.send: Common mix-up: A big sample is not the same as a good sample. If the method is biased (asking only your friends, scooping only from the top of the jar), even a huge sample will be off in the same direction. The key to a random sample is that every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen.

clips.send: Worked example: in a random sample of 50 students from a school of 600, 18 named soccer as their favourite sport. Sample proportion: 18 over 50 equals 36 percent . Estimate for the whole school: 0.36 times 600 equals 216 students. It is an estimate, not an exact count.

clips.send: Repeat it 40 times. Each dot is one random sample of 20 beads, placed at its percentage of red. The dots pile up into a hill: most samples land near the middle, but some are far off.

clips.send: Reveal the truth: 90 of the 300 beads are red, exactly 30 percent. Both piles are centered near 30 percent. That is inference: the proportion in a random sample is a fair estimate of the proportion in the population.

clips.send: But beware of bias. These red beads were poured in last and the jar was never shaken, so they sit near the top. Grab the 20 beads on top and 17 are red: 85 percent! When not every bead has an equal chance, the sample is biased, and repeating it never fixes that.
clips.text: But beware of bias. These red beads were poured in last and the jar was never shaken, so they sit near the top. Grab the 20 beads on top and 17 are red: 85%! When not every bead has an equal chance, the sample is biased, and repeating it never fixes that.

clips.send: Instead, take a random sample: shake the jar and pull out 20 beads without looking, so every bead has the same chance of being picked. This handful has 6 red out of 20, so we estimate hat p equals 6 over 20 equals 30 percent red.

clips.send: Put them back, shake, and draw again. This time 9 of 20 are red: 45 percent. Two random samples, two different answers! This natural wobble from sample to sample is called sampling variability.

clips.send: 比较两组：不施肥，A，与施肥，B，的植物高度，每组随机选 10 株。A 组平均数 11 厘米，B 组 15 厘米，两组的平均绝对偏差，M A D，都是 1.4 厘米。两组中心相差 4 厘米，接近 3 个 MAD，两堆点重叠很少：肥料看来确实有效。
clips.text: 比较两组：不施肥（A）与施肥（B）的植物高度，每组随机选 10 株。A 组平均数 11 厘米，B 组 15 厘米，两组的平均绝对偏差（MAD）都是 1.4 厘米。两组中心相差 4 厘米，接近 3 个 MAD，两堆点重叠很少：肥料看来确实有效。

clips.send: 重复 40 次。每个点代表一个容量为 20 的随机样本，放在它的红珠百分比处。这些点堆成一座“小山”：大多数样本落在中间附近，但也有一些偏得很远。
clips.text: 重复 40 次。每个点代表一个容量为 20 的随机样本，放在它的红珠百分比处。这些点堆成一座“小山”：大多数样本落在中间附近，但也有一些偏得很远。

clips.send: 例题：从一所 600 人的学校里随机抽取 50 名学生，其中 18 人最喜欢足球。样本比例： 50分之18 等于 百分之36 。估计全校： 0.36 乘 600 等于 216 人。这是估计值，不是精确的人数。

clips.send: 换个办法：随机抽样。摇匀罐子，闭着眼睛抓出 20 颗，让每颗珠子被抓到的机会都相同。这一把里 20 颗中有 6 颗红色，所以估计红珠比例 hat p 等于 20分之6 等于 百分之30 。
clips.text: 换个办法：随机抽样。摇匀罐子，闭着眼睛抓出 20 颗，让每颗珠子被抓到的机会都相同。这一把里 20 颗中有 6 颗红色，所以估计红珠比例 p 等于 20分之6 等于 30 % 。

clips.send: 容易混淆：样本大不等于样本好：如果抽样方法有偏差（比如只调查自己的朋友、只从罐子顶部抓），样本再大也会系统性地偏离真实情况。随机抽样的关键是：总体中每个个体被抽到的机会都相等。

clips.send: 但要当心偏差。这些红珠是最后倒进去的，罐子也没摇过，所以它们大多在上面。直接从顶部抓 20 颗，其中 17 颗是红的：百分之85！如果不是每颗珠子被抓到的机会都相等，样本就有偏差，而且重复多少次也改不掉。

clips.send: 把珠子放回去，摇匀，再抓一次。这次 20 颗中有 9 颗红色：百分之45。两个随机样本，两个不同的结果！样本与样本之间这种自然的波动，叫作抽样的变异性。

clips.send: 这个罐子里有 300 颗珠子，其中有些是红色的。整罐珠子就是总体。红珠占多大比例？当然可以一颗颗地数，但对于真实世界的总体（全国所有选民、湖里所有的鱼），这根本做不到。
